governance.note: Builds on the nyiso-33 ct-tempfloor keeper (byte-identical flags + the temperature-keyed downstate CT_PEAKER floor) and adds ONE new structural mechanism plus ONE benchmark-basis fix. NEW MECHANISM: a temperature-keyed downstate ST_GAS (gas-steam) local-reliability floor (--nyiso-st-reliability-floor, transmission.inject_nyiso_st_reliability_floor), the ST-fleet companion to the CT floor. MECHANISM: NYISO's downstate steam fleet (NYC zone J Ravenswood/Arthur Kill/Astoria; Long Island zone K; the Capital region) runs a persistent in-city / cable-islanded reliability baseline PLUS a strong summer cooling hot-limb that an energy-only LP zeroes out (it imports cheaper upstate/NYC combined cycle instead), so the backcast under-runs ST_GAS. The floor is a PERSISTENT 24-hour baseline (base_24h, applied over ALL hours -- the in-city must-run the measured cool-day CF shows running ~80% as high overnight as in the evening) with the evening cooling hot-limb layered on top over HB14-21 via maximum: overnight/midday frac=base_24h; evening frac=max(base_24h, clip(base_ev+slope*(TMAX-T0), base_ev, cap)). DISTRIBUTION (important): the hourly fraction is applied PER UNIT, PRO-RATA -- each in-pocket ST_GAS unit is floored at frac x its OWN available capacity, NOT cheapest-first over an aggregate target. In-city local reliability commits the geographically-distributed steam units (Ravenswood, Astoria, Arthur Kill -- each in its own NYC load pocket) by their locational role, so frac is a per-unit fleet CF; the measured CAMPD distribution confirms all the in-pocket steam runs at similar moderate CFs, NOT concentrated on the single cheapest unit. (A cheapest-first aggregate -- the initial implementation -- poured the whole NYC commitment into Ravenswood, the one unit an energy-only LP already runs economically, so the floor was redundant there and left the costlier Astoria/Arthur Kill idle; per-unit pro-rata is the physically-faithful and measured-distribution-matching form.) GROUNDING (a physical temperature->commitment rule, NOT a residual fit or a CEMS pin): the measured per-zone CAMPD ST_GAS fleet capacity factor regressed on the zone's load-center daily max temperature (NOAA GHCN: Islip for Long Island, Central Park for NYC, Albany for the Capital region), pooled 2023-2025 (scripts/derive_nyiso_st_reliability_floor.py, archived data/raw/nyiso-weather/nyiso_zone_tmax_daily.csv). Per-zone coefficients (transmission.NYISO_ST_FLOOR_COEFFS): base_24h cool-day all-hours p25, base_ev cool-day evening p25, cap evening p97, slope evening hot-limb -- Long Island base_24h 0.148 / base_ev 0.191 / slope 0.0588 / cap 0.851 (corr +0.63); NYC base_24h 0.105 / base_ev 0.112 / slope 0.0729 / cap 0.836 (corr +0.48); Capital hot-limb only base 0.0 / slope 0.0400 / cap 0.419 (weak, corr +0.089). The flat/temperature-insensitive Upstate steam fleet is deliberately OMITTED. All coefficients were set a priori from the regression BEFORE the solve; ST_GAS lands UNDER actual on the largest-miss scored year (2024 -1.45 TWh), and the floor lifts the costlier in-city units only to their conservative p25 baseline (Astoria/Arthur Kill remain under actual), so it is NOT over-forced and NOT pinned (rules #11/#12). The base x available-capacity basis is automatically outage-aware. FORWARD-REPRODUCIBLE: a forecast year pins a weather year (hence a per-zone TMAX series) exactly as it pins load/wind/solar. CAPACITY-DERATE CHECK (this session): the under-running in-city units are NOT capacity-capped -- they reach 0.66-0.92x nameplate in summer CAMPD and sit at model summer CF 0.02-0.17 with ample available headroom, i.e. idle (not dispatched), not derated. So the under-run is a dispatch/offer-curve effect, addressed by the distributed reliability floor, not a ceiling to lift. EFFECT vs the nyiso-33 keeper -- the HARD C1 fuel-mix improves: ST_GAS 2023 +1.12 TWh (PASS), 2024 -3.77 -> -1.45 TWh (recovers ~2.3 TWh; still under band, an honest MODEL MISS -- see _st_floor_status); CC_REGULAR 2023/24 -0.58/-0.56 (PASS); CT_PEAKER stays PASS (-0.93/-0.88); dispatch_corr stays PASS (gas r ~0.91/0.84/0.80); C5a CO2 returns to band both years. BENCHMARK-BASIS FIX (Task A, reporting only -- not a model lever): NYISO solar actuals now route to EIA-923 (results.calibration.actuals_source is ISO-aware). EIA-930 NYIS grid solar is a structural 0 (NYISO solar is overwhelmingly behind-the-meter / net-metered), so the dashboard previously scored the model's ~2 TWh of dispatched utility-scale grid solar against a spurious zero; the EIA-923 utility-scale total (2.05/2.90 TWh for 2023/2024) is now the actual on both the classFull and the e930-slot benchmark parts. The C3a/C3b/C3c price tradeoff is documented in the exceptions and kept per rule #1: the steam floor is a min-gen (must-run) representation that recovers the local-reliability ENERGY but adds inframarginal supply, depressing the marginal LMP rather than letting the units set a scarcity price.

_st_floor_status: The downstate ST_GAS under-run -- the largest remaining C1 (HARD) miss on the nyiso-33 keeper (2024 -3.77 TWh) -- is SUBSTANTIALLY reduced (2024 -3.77 -> -1.45 TWh) by a grounded, measured, forward-reproducible per-unit temperature floor, and 2023 ST_GAS lands in band (+1.12 PASS). The residual is left as an honest, UN-LEDGERED MODEL MISS (fuelmix C1 FAIL -> determination NOT-YET). TWO components remain, both named not chased: (1) the 2024 under-run is concentrated in the costlier in-city / Capital units (Astoria, Arthur Kill, Bowline) and the broad winter/shoulder months -- the deep-winter steam run is the gas-electric constraint (pipeline scarcity pricing dual-fuel steam into merit), the dual-fuel / Transco-Z6 gas-basis frontier, a SEPARATE structural lever from a cooling-driven floor; pushing the floor's p25 base higher to close it would over-force a cooling mechanism for a gas-constraint phenomenon (forbidden, rules #1/#11/#12). (2) Ravenswood (plant 2500, the most efficient NYC steam, corrected base HR 9.5 via data.fleet.MIXED_FACILITY_STEAM_HR) over-runs ECONOMICALLY in the transmission-constrained NYC zone (2023 +1.76, 2024 +0.21 TWh gross): as the cheapest in-city steam it clears as near-baseload, where the real fleet spreads the in-city commitment more evenly across Ravenswood/Astoria/Arthur Kill (each CAMPD CF ~0.18-0.23). The per-unit pro-rata floor lifts the costlier units toward that even distribution (Northport now exact, Arthur Kill/Astoria recovered, Ravenswood no longer floor-concentrated) but does not by itself cap Ravenswood's economic baseload; raising Ravenswood's cost to trim it would shift NYC load to CC/imports and push the steam class further under (the class is net under), so it is named as an NYC in-city-commitment / offer-curve residual, not forced. The C3a mean-LMP (2023/24/25 -14.9/-17.0/-12.7%) and empty C3c >$300 tail remain the ledgered reserve-scarcity (ORDC) frontier (min-gen floors add inframarginal supply but do not restore scarcity price-setting; non-closable with grounded inputs per nyiso-29/31), and the steam floor regresses them further as the documented rule-#1 tradeoff (kept, not chased). 2025 is preliminary-vintage (per-class skipped).

exceptions.metric: C3a system load-weighted mean LMP vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. The downstate ST_GAS floor, like the CT floor, is a min-gen (must-run) representation: it correctly recovers the local-reliability ENERGY (per-unit pro-rata across the in-city fleet) but adds inframarginal steam supply in the floored hours, depressing the marginal LMP rather than letting the units SET a high scarcity price. The fuller fix -- units setting price in scarcity hours via an ORDC/reserve-scarcity demand curve -- is the documented reserve-scarcity frontier (same root cause as the C3c >$300 tail), confirmed non-closable with grounded inputs by nyiso-29/31. Kept per rule #1: the floor is the real local-RA mechanism and closes most of the HARD C1 ST_GAS miss while fixing the plant-level distribution; reverting it to recover price would re-open the larger volume miss. Not chased (rule #12) -- the floor lifts the in-city units only to their conservative cool-day p25 baseline and ST_GAS still lands under actual in 2024.

exceptions.metric: C3a system load-weighted mean LMP vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. As 2023, with the largest depression because 2024 is the year the model most under-ran downstate steam, so the per-unit floor binds on the most idle in-city capacity (Astoria/Arthur Kill). Same ledgered root cause (reserve scarcity, nyiso-29/31): the recovered energy is correct but adds inframarginal supply, exposing the missing scarcity price tail. Kept per rule #1; not chased (rule #12) -- the base is the conservative cool-day p25 and ST_GAS still lands -1.45 TWh UNDER actual, so the price depression is the structural min-gen-floor consequence, not a too-high base.

exceptions.metric: C3a system load-weighted mean LMP vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. Same min-gen inframarginal-supply effect as 2023/2024. The downstate steam energy is correctly recovered; the price side is the ledgered reserve-scarcity frontier. Kept per rule #1; not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C3b price duration / shape NRMSE vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. The per-unit min-gen ST_GAS floor compresses the merit order and flattens the price duration curve (the high-price evening hours soften), the same root cause as the C3a/C3c reserve-scarcity frontier. 2023 (0.185) and 2025 (0.199) stay in band. Kept per rule #1; not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C3c scarcity tail (>$300/MWh hour count) vs actual RT
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. The >$300 scarcity tail is the canonical reserve-scarcity (ORDC) frontier: an energy-only LP with min-gen reliability floors recovers the local-RA energy but cannot form the scarcity price tail without an ORDC / reserve-scarcity demand curve that lets peakers/steam SET price in shortage. Confirmed non-closable with grounded inputs by nyiso-29/31. The steam floor adds inframarginal supply, if anything thinning the tail further -- the documented rule-#1 tradeoff. Named, not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C3c scarcity tail (>$300/MWh hour count) vs actual RT
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. Same ledgered reserve-scarcity (ORDC) frontier as 2023: the scarcity tail needs an ORDC / reserve-scarcity demand curve (out of scope, nyiso-29/31). Named, not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C3c scarcity tail (>$300/MWh hour count) vs actual RT
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. Same ledgered reserve-scarcity (ORDC) frontier as 2023/2024. Named, not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family total vs EIA-930 grid (preliminary vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (preliminary EIA-923 / EIA-930 benchmark-basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2025 EIA-923 is the preliminary M-file (total under-reported); the C2 family gate falls back to the EIA-930 grid total, against which the model gas total sits ~-3.5% at its benchmark-basis floor. The ST_GAS floor is a within-gas reshuffle (steam up, CC down) and does not move the gas TOTAL. Not closable by an honest knob (rules #1/#11/#12).
